facts.statement: Saltriovenator is a ceratosaurian dinosaur that lived in Italy during the Early Jurassic Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Saltriovenator (meaning "Saltrio hunter") is a genus of ceratosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic in what is now Italy.

facts.statement: The only known species of Saltriovenator is Saltriovenator zanellai.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Saltriovenator zanellai

facts.statement: Saltriovenator was likely a large, bipedal carnivore similar to Ceratosaurus, though no complete skeleton has been found.
facts.quote: Although a full skeleton has not yet been discovered, Saltriovenator is thought to have been a large, bipedal carnivore similar to Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: The first remains of Saltriovenator were discovered on August 4, 1996, by amateur paleontologist Angelo Zanella in a marble quarry in Saltrio, Italy.
facts.quote: On 4 August 1996, the first remains of Saltriovenator were discovered by amateur paleontologist Angelo Zanella, searching for ammonites in the Salnova marble quarry in Saltrio, northern Italy.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator zanellai was formally named and described in December 2018 by Dal Sasso, Maganuco, and Cau.
facts.quote: In December 2018, Dal Sasso, Simone Maganuco and Andrea Cau named and described the specimen as the type species Saltriovenator zanellai.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the earliest Early Sinemurian, approximately 199 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, MSNM V3664, was found in a layer of the Saltrio Formation dating from the earliest early Sinemurian, 199 million years old.

facts.statement: Only about 10% of the skeleton is known, consisting of various limb bones, ribs, a jaw fragment, and a furcula.
facts.quote: About 10% of the skeleton has been discovered, including a tooth, a right splenial, a right prearticular, a neck rib, fragments of the dorsal ribs and scapulae, a well preserved but incomplete furcula, humeri, metacarpal II, phalanx II-1, phalanx III-1, phalanx III-2, manual ungual III, a distal tarsal III, a distal tarsal IV and the proximal second to fifth metatarsals.

facts.statement: The fossil skeleton was shattered by explosives used in quarrying before it could be recovered.
facts.quote: The skeleton had shortly before its discovery been blown to pieces by explosives used in the quarry to break the marble layers.

facts.statement: Evidence of scratches and grooves on the bones indicates scavenging by marine invertebrates after death.
facts.quote: Various scratches, grooves, and striations indicate that the carcass was subject to scavenging by marine invertebrates.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator is considered the largest known theropod before the Aalenian stage, being 25% longer than the Late Jurassic Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: This would make Saltriovenator the largest known theropod living before the Aalenian stage, 25% longer than Ceratosaurus from the late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Estimated thighbone lengths indicate a body weight between 1,160 and 1,524 kilograms.
facts.quote: The thighbone length would then have been about eighty to eighty-seven centimetres, which indicates a body weight of 1160 to 1524 kilogrammes.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis in 2018 identified Saltriovenator as a basal ceratosaur and the sister-taxon of Berberosaurus.
facts.quote: The 2018 description paper ran a large phylogenetic analysis, and found it to be a basal ceratosaur, the sister-taxon of Berberosaurus.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in an open marine environment, likely washed from the mainland and scavenged by invertebrates.
facts.quote: Saltriovenator was found on an open marine environment, where it was probably washed from the nearest mainland, being scavenged by invertebrates as proven by the presence of Sedilichnus sp. on the bones.

facts.statement: During the Late Hettangian to Early Sinemurian, the region was part of the Southern Alps passive margin of Adria, characterized by alternating shallow platforms and subsiding troughs.
facts.quote: During the late Hettangian to early Sinemurian, the western Lombardy Basin formed part of the Southern Alps area, passive margin of Adria and formed part of an evolving rift system linked to the western Tethys, where horst-and-graben tectonics created alternating shallow platforms and subsiding troughs.

facts.statement: Fossil pollen indicates a tropical subhumid climate with forests dominated by Hirmeriellaceae and fern understories.
facts.quote: Palynological assemblages from these horizons indicate Hirmeriellaceae-dominated forests and understory of Lycopsid-Ferns, as well potential Characeae, adapted to marsh or ponded settings in a Tropical subhumid climate.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator was likely the largest predator in its region.
facts.quote: This theropod was probably the largest predator on the region.

facts.statement: The first remains of Saltriovenator were discovered on August 4, 1996, by amateur paleontologist Angelo Zanella.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Saltriovenator fueron descubiertos el 4 de agosto de 1996 por el paleontólogo aficionado Angelo Zanella

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, MSNM V3664, was found in the Saltrio Formation dating to the early Sinemurian, 199 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, MSNM V3664, fue hallado en una capa de la Formación Saltrio la cual data de principios del Sinemuriense, hace 199 millones de años.

facts.statement: Dal Sasso, Maganuco, and Cau named and described the species Saltriovenator zanellai in December 2018.
facts.quote: En diciembre de 2018, Dal Sasso, Simone Maganuco y Andrea Cau nombraron y describieron al espécimen como la especie tipo Saltriovenator zanellai.

facts.statement: Although no complete skeleton has been found, Saltriovenator is believed to have been a large, bipedal carnivore similar to Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque todavía no se ha descubierto un esqueleto completo,se cree que Saltriovenator era un carnívoro grande y bípedo similar a Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers conservatively estimated the holotype individual of Saltriovenator to be between seven and eight meters in length.
facts.quote: ellos concluyeron de forma conservadora que el individuo holotipo de Saltriovenator medía entre siete a ocho metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator would be the largest theropod that lived before the Aalenian epoch, 25% longer than Upper Jurassic Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: Esto convertiría a Saltriovenator en el mayor terópodo que vivió antes de la época del Aaleniense, 25% más largo que Ceratosaurus del Jurásico Superior.

facts.statement: The femur would have been between 80 and 87 centimeters long, indicating a body weight of 1160 to 1524 kilograms.
facts.quote: El fémur habría sido de entre 80 a 87 centímetros, lo cual indica un peso corporal de 1160 a 1524 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The specimen corresponds to a subadult individual near its maximum size, estimated to be about twenty-four years old.
facts.quote: El espécimen corresponde a un individuo subadulto, cercano a su tamaño máximo, cuya edad se ha estimado en unos veinticuatro años.

facts.statement: Various scars, grooves, and striations indicate that the carcass was consumed by marine invertebrate scavengers.
facts.quote: Varias cicatrices, surcos y estrías indican que el cadáver fue consumido por invertebrados marinos carroñeros.

facts.statement: A 2018 phylogenetic analysis determined Saltriovenator to be a basal ceratosaurian, being the sister taxon to Berberosaurus.
facts.quote: El artículo de descripción publicado en 2018 llevó a cabo un gran análisis filogenético, y determinó que se trataba de un ceratosaurio basal, siendo el taxón hermano de Berberosaurus.

facts.statement: Dal Sasso originally classified Saltriovenator among the Tetanurae but later considered it might represent an allosauroid.
facts.quote: Dal Sasso originalmente lo clasificó entre los Tetanurae. Él más tarde consideró que podría representar un alosauroideo

facts.statement: Benson considered Saltriovenator to be a member of Coelophysoidea in his review of Magnosaurus.
facts.quote: Benson lo consideró como un miembro de Coelophysoidea en su revisión de Magnosaurus.

facts.statement: Although Saltriovenator was not aquatic, the environment where the carcass was deposited was likely pelagic, judging by associated ammonites.
facts.quote: Aunque Saltriovenator no era acuático, el ambiente en que se depósito el cadáver probablemente era pelágico, al juzgar por los ammonites asociados.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator likely lived in an open marine environment where it was dragged from the nearest continent and eaten by invertebrates, evidenced by Sedilichnus sp. bite marks on its bones.
facts.quote: Saltrioventor se encontró en un ambiente marino abierto, donde probablemente fue arrastrado desde el continente más cercano, siendo devorado por invertebrados como lo demuestra la presencia de Sedilichnus sp. en los huesos.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator lived in the western Lombardy basin from the early Jurassic, spanning the Hettangian to early Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Desde el comienzo del Jurásico, desde Hettangiense hasta principios del Sinemuriense en la cuenca occidental de Lombardía.

facts.statement: A significant continental area existed near the fossil site with a previously underestimated size, characterized by a warm and humid paleoclimate.
facts.quote: Hubo un área continental notoria que resultó ser más amplia de lo que se pensaba anteriormente, donde se desarrolló un paleoclima cálido húmedo.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Saltriovenator originated from a nearby landmass rather than distant emergent zones like the Trento Platform.
facts.quote: Saltriovenator probablemente provienen de esta masa de tierra cercana, ya que otras zonas emergidas, como la Plataforma de Trento, estaban lejos de la ubicación del descubrimiento.

facts.statement: If it originated from the nearby landmass, Saltriovenator was likely the largest predator in the region.
facts.quote: Si es así, este terópodo fue probablemente el depredador más grande de la región.

facts.statement: Saltriovenator is classified within the parent group Ceratosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratosauria

facts.statement: Saltriovenator belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Saltriovenator is Saltriovenator zanellai.
facts.quote: Type species: Saltriovenator zanellai

facts.statement: The genus Saltriovenator was named by Dal Sasso and colleagues in 2018.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Saltriovenator (genus), Dal Sasso et al. 2018

facts.statement: Saltriovenator lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The specimen represents a subadult individual, nearing its maximum size, of which the age has been estimated at twenty-four years.
